counterfactual_missing_items: Premature atrial complex preceding onset of arrhythmia
decisive_items: Severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction, ejection fraction 15-20%
Abrupt changes in heart rates while at rest, lasting few minutes
response.rationale: R5 uniquely links the atrial tachycardia to the severe LV systolic dysfunction via a causal mechanism, explaining the entire clinical picture. R7 captures only the cardiomyopathy, while R6/R4 capture only the arrhythmia. The temporal relationship and absence of CAD support tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy as the unifying diagnosis.

rejected.why: Redundant completion of R5; adds no diagnostic information beyond the parent diagnosis
Describes the cardiomyopathy but fails to explain the underlying tachycardia as the cause
Captures the arrhythmia and dysfunction but lacks the etiological link of tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy
Only addresses the atrial tachycardia and ignores the severe LV systolic dysfunction
Narrows the diagnosis to a subtype of atrial tachycardia without addressing the cardiomyopathy
Adds a vague descriptor of cardiac dysfunction without the specific etiological mechanism
Merely adds 'severe' to HFrEF, which is already implied by the EF of 15-20%
